description: A single-panel engineering stress–strain plot, labelled (a), for the 0.02Nb steel. Y-axis is "Engineering stress (MPa)" from 0 to 1400 in 200 MPa increments; X-axis is "Engineering strain (%)" from 0 to 50 in 10 % increments. The panel contains four curves distinguished by a legend in the lower right: "as-cast" (black), "723 K/3 h" (red), "773 K/3 h" (blue) and "823 K/3 h" (green). All curves show a steep elastic rise followed by a flat, slowly rising plastic plateau with no pronounced stress peak. The green 823 K/3 h curve reaches the highest stress (peaking near the 1100–1200 MPa gridlines) but terminates at the smallest strain, near 8 %; the blue 773 K/3 h curve ends near 17–18 % strain, the red 723 K/3 h curve near 31 %, and the black as-cast curve extends furthest, to roughly 38 % strain. The plateau stresses of as-cast, 723 K/3 h and 773 K/3 h lie close together around the 1000–1050 MPa level, in contrast to the higher but much less ductile 823 K/3 h condition. The figure demonstrates that aging treatment, especially at 823 K/3 h, raises strength at the cost of ductility relative to the as-cast state. Panel (b) for the 0.04Nb steel, promised by the caption, is not present in this image.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an engineering stress–strain plot with y-axis 'Engineering stress (MPa)' spanning 0–1400 MPa (200 MPa ticks) and x-axis 'Engineering strain (%)' spanning 0–50 % (10 % ticks).
The legend lists four conditions: 'as-cast' (black), '723 K/3 h' (red), '773 K/3 h' (blue) and '823 K/3 h' (green).
The green 823 K/3 h curve attains the highest engineering stress, peaking between the 1100 and 1200 MPa gridlines.
The 823 K/3 h (green) curve terminates at the smallest strain, near 8 %, indicating the lowest ductility of the four conditions.
The as-cast (black) curve extends to the largest strain, roughly 38 %, with a plateau stress near the 1000–1050 MPa level.
The 773 K/3 h (blue) and 723 K/3 h (red) curves terminate near 17–18 % and ~31 % strain respectively, both at plateau stresses close to the as-cast curve.
The stress–strain curves show a steep elastic rise followed by a flat, slowly rising plateau with no pronounced peak stress before failure.
The caption states the figure presents engineering stress–strain curves of the a) 0.02Nb and b) 0.04Nb steels.
Only panel (a), the 0.02Nb steel, is present in the supplied image; panel (b) for 0.04Nb is missing or not rendered.
